events.text_en: Băng Tâm Các leaves its desert pavilion and raises its halls on the ruin of Hồ Thiên Phái, on the ice the fire mountain buried.
Tần Ngưng Sương lays the Jade Vessel Array into the ice over the buried vent; the steam stops, and the birds come back to Ngọc Hồ Sơn.
A four-year-old boy is carried out of the ruin of Cô Thành wrapped in his dead father's cape, a red-ink sword manual sewn into the lining: the last of Lãnh Hương Các.
Passed over for the Vessel, Cố Lăng Sương climbs Băng Bích Nhai the winter her master dies and closes the cave behind her.
Hạng Dạ Bôi's son Hạng Minh Sa, twenty-one, is sent to Băng Tâm Các as surety for his father's knee.
